diagram_math_checks.evidence: r=2; A0=(0,0), A1=(0,2), E0=(3,2), E1=(3,4). Paths satisfy def-path-system-and-non-intersecting-path-system; every consecutive difference is E=(1,0) or N=(0,1), checked computationally against def-monotone-lattice-path.

Left blue vertices: (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(3,2); left orange: (0,2),(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,4),(3,4). Right blue: (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(2,4),(3,4); right orange: (0,2),(1,2),(2,2),(3,2). Each panel has 11 distinct marked path vertices and 10 directed unit edges, with one final arrow per path. Gray grid is a coordinate guide. No closed path is asserted: coordinate sum strictly increases on every directed edge, so the path union is acyclic.

Enumerated both pairs of vertex lists: the shared-vertex set is exactly {(1,2)} before and after. Thus it is the lexicographically least shared vertex and (0,1) is the unique index pair in supplier proof step 1.1. Prefixes end at x and the two displayed suffixes exchange exactly as supplier steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1; swapping again restores the left panel.

Left endpoints are A0 to E0 and A1 to E1 (identity, sign +1); right endpoints are A0 to E1 and A1 to E0 (transposition (0 1), sign -1). This is pi prime = pi composed with (0 1), as supplier step 2.2. Each displayed system is a single unit-count term in theorem proof step 2.1, so +1 and -1 cancel in step 3.1. No compatible-configuration claim or weighted/general-DAG theorem is added.

Viewed both final PNG tiles individually at original resolution. All 11 marked vertices and ten path segments per panel are present; sources and sinks, x labels, terminal arrows and sign labels are legible and separated. No closure edge or between-vertex crossing exists.
